prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / view derivation. Create a FOUR-VIEW design sheet of the EXACT BOMBER AIRCRAFT in the input, not a new aircraft. Landscape canvas, clean ivory background, four clearly separated equal panels in a 2 by 2 arrangement: upper-left FRONT head-on; upper-right exact LEFT SIDE profile with nose pointing LEFT; lower-left TOP plan with nose pointing LEFT; lower-right REAR head-on. Orthographic-looking projection, no perspective three-quarter views, no labels, no diagrams over the vehicle, no human/robot parts. Precise KINETIC_CEL ink and cel colors matching the source.

Identity lock across all views: ONE short blunt orange faceted nose with wide blue-black canopy and ivory cheek frames; ONE central low fuselage with orange-framed dark machinery vent pack; TWO huge laterally spread swept triangular graphite main wings with ivory leading edges and thin orange strips; TWO cylindrical underwing engines with silver front intake rims, orange bands and dark nacelle bodies; TWO narrow upright graphite tail fins with orange edges on the aft central-fuselage shoulder roots, inboard of main wings. Main wings attach through clearly separate circular root pivots, with no additional central wing or third engine. Preserve every major count, attachment location, material/color division and front/back direction.

FRONT: nose and canopy between two engine INTAKES with visible forward fans, two upright aft fins visible above the fuselage, main wings thin in elevation. SIDE: nose left, tail right, the near engine runs fore-aft under its wing and shows its CYLINDRICAL SIDE, never an outward-facing fan disk; two tail fins can overlap naturally, do not rotate the main wing upright. TOP: show the same nose/canopy left, rear pack and two slim longitudinal fin edges right, swept wings spread laterally, engine locations consistent with underside mounting. REAR: two outboard engines show recessed DARK EXHAUST nozzles, not front-facing intake fan disks; central orange-framed stacked rectangular grilles remain distinct between the two tail fins. Keep a common coherent wing span, fuselage length, engine radius and tail-fin height; use subtle alignment cues if useful. High clarity same-object design sheet, no redesign or extra weapons.
